key_insight: For linear elastostatics, minimizing discrete potential energy is equivalent to supervised learning in the energy norm, aligning surrogate training with stress accuracy rather than displacement accuracy.
engineering_relevance: Energy-norm training improves stress predictions for perforated plates and solids with cavities, where holes concentrate stress.
method: Train finite-element surrogates using energy-norm supervision or discrete potential energy without solution labels.
Evaluate energy-norm and stress errors alongside displacement errors.
Use potential energy to rank predictions for a load case and flag those worse than the zero field.
evidence_signal: In pre-registered comparisons, changing only the supervised loss norm reduced a 3D transformer's median energy-norm error 7.5-fold and median von Mises error 6.1-fold; 2D von Mises error more than halved.
watch_item: No tested network transferred to a substantially finer mesh, limiting claims of mesh generalization.
paper_title: The norm, not the labels: training and evaluating finite-element surrogates for stress analysis in the energy norm
